To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the communication range in wireless sensor networks is highly variable and that it is not possible to predict the reception rate of a packet based on the distance between transmitter and receiver.
the relationship between distance and reception rate can be characterized by a probability density function.

the probability density function of the communication quality of a link in a sensor network is a function of the distance between the transmitter and the receiver and the number of obstacles between these two nodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of statistical techniques and models to improve wireless network simulation and to extract knowledge from wireless network experiments.
the development of a statistical framework that allows the extraction of communication properties from empirical data and the generation of wireless sensor network models with realistic properties.
the statistical analysis of empirical communication data and its use for the development of simulation models that produce realistic wireless networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can provide a statistical model for the lossy wireless links in a wireless sensor network and that we can use it to generate realistic network models.
the communication properties of wireless sensor networks are strongly correlated with the location of the transmitters and receivers.
the use of widely used simulation models for wireless sensor networks is not appropriate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to generate realistic wireless sensor networks that are statistically equivalent to real networks and that we can predict the performance of wireless sensor networks using statistical techniques.
the communication properties of wireless sensor networks are highly dependent on the location of the transmitters and receivers.
the use of a statistical approach to model wireless sensor network links is an important step towards realistic simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the statistical analysis of wireless networks is essential to draw conclusions from experimental studies and that the proposed models are a valuable tool to evaluate the performance of wireless sensor network protocols.
the use of statistical techniques can significantly improve the accuracy of simulation models, and that this improvement is necessary in order to draw sound conclusions.
the statistical model of the link properties is an essential tool to analyze and predict the behavior of wireless sensor networks.
